text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgarians have withdrawn some $800 million from their accounts in local commercial banks last year because of low confidence in the banking systam, Bulgarian National Bank figures showed.

-- The Bulgarian lev may fall sharply when foreign investors who have invested in Bulgarian government securities decide to convert their investments into dollars if yield on the paper continues to fall, bank experts said.
-- Bulgaria's Foreign minister Stoyan Stalev left for Paris to attend a meeting of the Western European Union where NATO's enlargement to the East was expected to be discussed.
-- Bulgaria's Geology and Mineral Resources Committee said it would open tenders for eight concessions for oil research and oil production in Northern Bulgaria, private Balkan agency said. @

-- Creditors of Bulgaria's private refinery Plama may file a bankruptcy suit against it because of overdue debts totalling $111 million and seven billion levs, Bulgaria's private Central Cooperative Bank executive director Stoyan Alexandrov said in an interview with the national radio.

-- Bulgaria's consumer prices fell 0.7 percent month on month in April for the first time since Bulgaria launched market reforms in 1990, the National Statistics Institute said. Inflation was 12.3 percent in March and 242.7 percent in February. @
-- Bulgaria's gas monopolist Bulgargas said it would allow private gas firms to set prices for importing Russian natural gas to Bulgaria and would seek more favourable prices.
-- The United States granted 25 tonnes of humanitarian aid worth $2.1 million to Bulgaria.
-- The World Bank said it had approved a $40 million loan to Bulgaria for importing essential goods like grain, fuel and medical supplies.

-- The budget and economy committees at Bulgaria's parliament are expected to discuss today draft law amendments required to facilitate the introduction of a fixed exchange rate regime, called a currency board, in the country. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
